source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Review pneumococcal vaccination by age and history, but defer recombinant zoster vaccination because increasing age makes zoster vaccination inappropriate.","B":"Recommend recombinant zoster vaccine, but omit pneumococcal vaccination unless the client has previously been hospitalized for bacterial pneumonia.","C":"Continue influenza vaccination, but discontinue age-based zoster and pneumococcal vaccination because those vaccines are intended for younger adults.","D":"Review vaccine history and give indicated recombinant zoster and pneumococcal vaccines, plus other vaccines recommended by age, history, and risk level."}}
source_row.rationale: Older adulthood does not end routine vaccination. The current CDC adult schedule requires review of age, prior vaccination history, and risk factors; recombinant zoster and pneumococcal vaccines are among the vaccines routinely considered in this age range, along with other indicated vaccines. Option D appropriately directs history-based use of the current schedule. Options A, B, and C incorrectly exclude age-indicated vaccination or impose unsupported prerequisites.
source_row.source_detail: CDC — Adult Immunization Schedule by Age, current schedule: vaccination in older adults is based on age, prior doses/history and risk factors; the ≥65-year age rows/notes include indicated recombinant zoster and pneumococcal vaccination along with other age/risk-based vaccines. Current CDC adult schedule is the July 2, 2025 schedule as amended 2026-04-27 under the March 16, 2026 court order; current CDC schedule status live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Health Promotion and Maintenance: preventive care, immunization, pregnancy health promotion, adherence support and age/risk-appropriate teaching activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: A 68-year-old client asks which routine vaccinations still matter in older adulthood. Which response best reflects current CDC guidance?
